- Working diagnosis and impression: Urinary tract infection (cystitis) suspected with likely lower abdominal pain and per-urinary symptoms; pregnancy-related etiology to be excluded; planning empiric treatment and tests to refine diagnosis

  - Urinary tract infection (cystitis) – High likelihood: lower abdominal pain near bladder, pink urine, increased urination; clinician planned empiric trimethoprim and urine-related assessment
  - Early pregnancy-related pain (including risk of ectopic pregnancy) – Medium-High likelihood: recent sexual activity, last period ~2 weeks ago, implant contraception present; pregnancy test planned

- Plan details: Obtain testing to rule out pregnancy and other causes; empiric antibiotic therapy for possible UTI (trimethoprim) with follow-up in a few days; advise hydration and pain control; consider cranberry juice for urinary symptoms
- Considerations: Pregnancy test to exclude pregnancy-related causes; imaging not pursued at this visit; follow-up if symptoms worsen or do not improve
